verses.zh: 以色列人哪，当听耶和华的话！要起来向山岭争辩，使冈陵听你的话。
verses.en: Listen to what the Lord says:“Get up! Defend yourself[NOTE:1] before the mountains.[NOTE:2] Present your case before the hills.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Defend yourself. The Lord challenges Israel to defend itself against the charges he is bringing.tn Or “plead your case” (NASB, NIV84, NRSV); NAB “present your plea”; NLT “state your case”; NIV11 “plead my case.”
As in some ancient Near Eastern treaties, the mountains are personified as legal witnesses that will settle the dispute between God and Israel.
Heb “let the hills hear your voice.”

verses.zh: 山岭和地永久的根基啊，要听耶和华争辩的话！因为耶和华要与他的百姓争辩，与以色列争论。
verses.en: Hear the Lord’s accusation, you mountains,you enduring foundations of the earth.For the Lord has a case against his people;he has a dispute with Israel![NOTE:1]
notes: The prophet briefly interrupts the Lord’s statement (see vv. 1, 3) to summon the mountains as witnesses. Though the prophet speaks, the quotation marks have been omitted to clarify that it is not the Lord still speaking.

verses.zh: 我的百姓啊，我向你做了甚么呢？我在甚么事上使你厌烦？你可以对我证明。
verses.en: “My people, how have I wronged you?[NOTE:1] How have I wearied you? Answer me!
notes: Heb “My people, what have I done to you?”

verses.zh: 我曾将你从埃及地领出来，从作奴仆之家救赎你；我也差遣摩西、亚伦，和米利暗在你前面行。
verses.en: In fact, I brought you up from the land of Egypt;I delivered you from that place of slavery.I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to lead you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “before you.”

verses.zh: 我的百姓啊，你们当追念摩押王巴勒所设的谋和比珥的儿子巴兰回答他的话，并你们从什亭到吉甲所遇见的事，好使你们知道耶和华公义的作为。
verses.en: My people, recall how King Balak of Moab planned to harm you,[NOTE:1] how Balaam son of Beor responded to him.Recall how you journeyed from Shittim to Gilgal,so you might acknowledge that the Lord has treated you fairly.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “remember what Balak…planned.”

Heb “From Shittim to Gilgal, in order to know the just acts of the Lord.” Something appears to be missing at the beginning of the line. The present translation supplies the words, “Recall how you went.” This apparently refers to how Israel crossed the Jordan River (see Josh 3:1; 4:19-24).

verses.zh: 我朝见耶和华，在至高　神面前跪拜，当献上甚么呢？岂可献一岁的牛犊为燔祭吗？
verses.en: With what should I[NOTE:1] enter the Lord’s presence?With what[NOTE:2] should I bow before the sovereign God?[NOTE:3] Should I enter his presence with burnt offerings,with year-old calves?
notes: With what should I enter the Lord’s presence? The prophet speaks again, playing the role of an inquisitive worshiper who wants to know what God really desires from his followers.
The words “with what” do double duty in the parallelism and are supplied in the second line of the translation for clarification.
Or “the exalted God.”

verses.zh: 耶和华岂喜悦千千的公羊，或是万万的油河吗？我岂可为自己的罪过献我的长子吗？为心中的罪恶献我身所生的吗？
verses.en: Will the Lord accept a thousand ramsor ten thousand streams of olive oil?Should I give him my firstborn child as payment for my rebellion,my offspring—my own flesh and blood—for my sin?[NOTE:1]
notes: Since child sacrifice is forbidden in scripture (Deut 12:31; 18:10), the speaker is revealed to not be in earnest but perhaps sarcastic.tn Heb “the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul.” The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) is often translated “soul,” but the word usually refers to the whole person; here “the sin of my soul” = “my sin.”

verses.zh: 世人哪，耶和华已指示你何为善。他向你所要的是甚么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的　神同行。
verses.en: He has told you,[NOTE:1] O man, what is good,and what the Lord really wants from you:[NOTE:2] He wants you to[NOTE:3] carry out justice,[NOTE:4] to love faithfulness,[NOTE:5] and to live obediently before[NOTE:6] your God.
notes: Now the prophet switches roles and answers the question of the hypothetical worshiper. He rebukes the extravagant surface remark by pointing to general character qualities that are lacking in Israel.
Heb “is seeking from you.”
Heb “except.” This statement is actually linked with what precedes, “What does he want from you except….”
Or “to act justly.”

Or “to love faithfully.” The Hebrew word חֶסֶד (khesed) is complex, sometimes translated “lovingkindness,” faithfulness,” or “loyal love.” It has also been understood as covenant loyalty. חֶסֶד is either the object or the manner of the infinitive “to love.”
Heb “to walk humbly [or perhaps, “carefully”] with.”

verses.zh: 耶和华向这城呼叫，智慧人必敬畏他的名。你们当听是谁派定刑杖的惩罚。
verses.en: Listen! The Lord is calling[NOTE:1] to the city!It is wise to respect your authority, O Lord.[NOTE:2] Listen, O nation, and those assembled in the city![NOTE:3]
notes: Or “the voice of the Lord is calling.” The translation understands קוֹל (qol, “voice”) as equivalent to an imperative.

Heb “one who sees your name is wisdom.” It is probably better to emend יִרְאֶה (yirʾeh, “he sees”) to יִרְאָה (yirʾah, “fearing”). One may then translate, “fearing your name is wisdom.” The Lord’s “name” here stands by metonymy for his authority.

The MT reads, “Listen, tribe (or staff) and who appointed it.” Verse 10 then begins with עוֹד (ʿod, “still” or “again”). The LXX reads, “who will set the city in order?” The translation assumes an emendation of וּמִי יְעָדָהּ. עוֹד (umi yeʿadah. ʿod…, “and who appointed it. Still…”) to וּמוֹעֵד הָעִיר(umoʿed haʿir, “and the assembly of the city”).

verses.zh: 恶人家中不仍有非义之财和可恶的小升斗吗？
verses.en: “I will not overlook,[NOTE:1] O sinful house, the dishonest gain you have hoarded away[NOTE:2] or the smaller-than-standard measure I hate so much.[NOTE:3]
notes: The meaning of the first Hebrew word in the line is unclear. Possibly it is a combination of the interrogative particle and אִשׁ (ʾish), an alternate form of יֵשׁ (yesh, “there is/are”). One could then translate literally, “Are there treasures of sin [in] the house of the sinful?” The translation assumes an emendation to הַאֶשֶּׁה (haʾesheh, from נָשָׁא, nashaʾ, “to forget”), “Will I forget?” The rhetorical question expects an answer, “No, I will not forget.”
Heb “the treasures of sin”; NASB “treasures of wickedness”; NIV “ill-gotten treasures.”
Merchants would use a smaller than standard measure so they could give the customer less than he thought he was paying for.tn Heb “the accursed scant measure.”

verses.zh: 我若用不公道的天平和囊中诡诈的法码，岂可算为清洁呢？
verses.en: I do not condone the use of rigged scalesor a bag of deceptive weights.[NOTE:1]
notes: Merchants also used rigged scales and deceptive weights to cheat their customers. See the note at Amos 8:5.tn Heb “Do I acquit sinful scales, and a bag of deceptive weights?” The rhetorical question expects an answer, “No, I do not,” and has been translated as a declarative statement for clarity and emphasis.

verses.zh: 城里的富户满行强暴；其中的居民也说谎言，口中的舌头是诡诈的。
verses.en: The city’s wealthy people readily resort to violence;[NOTE:1] her inhabitants tell lies;their tongues speak deceptive words.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “are full of violence.”
Heb “and their tongue is deceptive in their mouth.”

verses.zh: 因此，我击打你，使你的伤痕甚重，使你因你的罪恶荒凉。
verses.en: I will strike you brutally[NOTE:1] and destroy you because of your sin.
notes: Heb “and I, even I, will make you sick, [by] striking you.”

verses.zh: 你要吃，却吃不饱；你的虚弱必显在你中间。你必挪去，却不得救护；所救护的，我必交给刀剑。
verses.en: You will eat, but not be satisfied.Even if you have the strength[NOTE:1] to overtake some prey,[NOTE:2] you will not be able to carry it away;[NOTE:3] if you do happen to carry away something, I will deliver it over to the sword.
notes: The first Hebrew term in the line (וְיֶשְׁחֲךָ, veyeshkhakha) is obscure. HALOT 446 s.v. יֶשַׁח understands a noun meaning “filth,” which would yield the translation, “and your filth is inside you.” The translation assumes an emendation to כֹּחַוְיֶשׁ (veyesh koakh, “and [if] there is strength inside you”).

The meaning of the Hebrew term וְתַסֵּג (vetasseg) is unclear. The translation assumes it is a Hiphal imperfect from נָסַג/נָשַׂג (nasag/nasag, “reach; overtake”) and that hunting imagery is employed. (Note the reference to hunger in the first line of the verse.) See D. R. Hillers, Micah (Hermeneia), 80.
The Hiphal of פָּלַט (palat) is used in Isa 5:29 of an animal carrying its prey to a secure place.

verses.zh: 你必撒种，却不得收割；踹橄榄，却不得油抹身；踹葡萄，却不得酒喝。
verses.en: You will plant crops, but will not harvest them;you will squeeze oil from the olives,[NOTE:1] but you will have no oil to rub on your bodies;[NOTE:2] you will squeeze juice from the grapes, but you will have no wine to drink.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you will tread olives.” Literally treading on olives with one’s feet could be harmful and would not supply the necessary pressure to release the oil. See O. Borowski, Agriculture in Iron Age Israel, 119. The Hebrew term דָּרַךְ (darakh) may have an idiomatic sense of “press” here, or perhaps the imagery of the following parallel line (referring to treading grapes) has dictated the word choice.
Heb “but you will not rub yourselves with oil.”
Heb “and juice, but you will not drink wine.” The verb תִדְרֹךְ (tidrokh, “you will tread”) must be supplied from the preceding line.

verses.zh: 因为你守暗利的恶规，行亚哈家一切所行的，顺从他们的计谋；因此，我必使你荒凉，使你的居民令人嗤笑，你们也必担当我民的羞辱。
verses.en: You follow Omri’s edicts[NOTE:1] and all the practices of Ahab’s dynasty;[NOTE:2] you follow their policies.[NOTE:3] Therefore I will make you an appalling sight;[NOTE:4] the city’s[NOTE:5] inhabitants will be taunted derisively,[NOTE:6] and nations will mock all of you.”[NOTE:7]
notes: Heb “the edicts of Omri are kept.”
Heb “the house of Ahab.”
The Omride dynasty, of which Ahab was the most infamous king, had a reputation for implementing unjust and oppressive measures. See 1 Kgs 21.tn Heb “and you walk in their plans.”
The Hebrew term שַׁמָּה (shammah) can refer to “destruction; ruin,” or to the reaction it produces in those who witness the destruction.
Heb “her.”
Heb “[an object] of hissing,” which was a way of taunting someone.

Heb “and the reproach of my people you will bear.” The second person verb is plural here, in contrast to the singular forms used in vv. 13-15.tc The translation assumes an emendation of the MT’s עַמִּי (ʿammi, “my people”) to עַמִּים (ʿammim, “nations”).

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

BRIEF OUTLINE OF CHAPTER 6

- YHWH brings His people to court in Micah 6:1-5. He documents His faithfulness to them in Micah 6:3-5.
This court imagery is a common literary device in the prophets (i.e. Isa. 1; Jer. 2: Hosea 4).

Special Topic: Prophecy (OT), IV. E.

- The people answer God's charges in Micah 6:6-7.

- The Prophet speaking for YHWH summarizes His will for His people in Micah 6:8

- The prophet speaking for YHWH delineates the sins of the rich and powerful of the descendants
of Abraham in Micah 6:9-16. Because of them the covenant curses of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28
are now invoked (i.e. Deut. 28:15,18,40,51). Oh my!

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: MICAH 6:1-5

1Hear now what the Lord is saying,

"Arise, plead your case before the mountains,

And let the hill hear your voice.

2Listen, you mountains, to the indictment of the Lord,

And you enduring foundations of the earth,

Because the Lord has a case against His people;

Even with Israel He will dispute.

3My people, what have I done to you

And how have I wearied you? Answer Me.

4Indeed, I brought you up from the land of Egypt

And ransomed you up from the house of slavery,

And I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

5My people, remember now

What Balak king of Moab counseled

And what Balaam son of Beor answered him,

And from Shittim to Gilgal,

In order that you might know the righteous acts of the Lord."

6:1-2 "Hear" There are several Qal IMPERATIVES in Micah 6:1-2:

- "Hear" (BDB 1033, KB 1570, i.e. in the sense of a prayer petition) ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE

- "Arise" (BDB 877, KB 1086) ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE

- "Plead your case" (DBD 936, KB 1224) ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE

- "Hear" (BDB 1033, KB 1570) ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE used in a JUSSIVE sense

- "Listen" (BDB 1033, KB 1570) ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE

"Hear" is a way for Micah to start a new section (cf. Micah 1:1; 3:1; 6:1).

The second IMPERATIVE
"arise" is MASCULINE SINGULAR. It could refer to Micah as YHWH's spokesman or collectively to the
nation. Option #1 fits the context best.

This chapter is a court scene. Notice the number of terms with a legal connotation:

- "Arise" (i.e. to testify, i.e. Deut. 19:15-16 and false witnesses in Ps. 27:12; 35:11), Micah 6:1

- "Plead" (i.e. to contend in court

- negatively, i.e. Isa. 1:17; 3:13; 97:16

- positively 7:9; Ps. 103:8-14, esp. 9; Jer. 50:34)

- "Hear" (i.e. in the sense of a jury or judge, i.e. Micah 1:2)

- "Listen" (same word as #3)

- "Indictment" (same word as #2)

- "A case" (same word as #3 and #5)

- "Dispute" (BDB 406, KB 410, Hithpael IMPERFECT, i.e. adjudication of a judge, i.e. Isa. 2:4; Micah 4:3)

YHWH is divorcing His covenant people because of their repeated unfaithfulness (Hosea) and sin
(Amos). This is the clear reality of a conditional covenant. This court scene may continue through Micah 7.

Special Topic: Listen/Hear (shema)

Special Topic: Covenant

Special Topic: YHWH's Covenant Requirements of Israel

▣ "before the mountains. . .hills" In the OT it takes two witnesses to confirm truth (cf. Num. 35:30;
Deut. 17:6; 19:5). YHWH calls

- "the mountains" and "hills" to witness against Israel and Judah

- as He does "heaven and earth" (cf. Deut. 4:26; 31:28; 32:l; Ps. 50:4 and Isa. 1:2)

- as He does , "O peoples. . .O earth" (cf. Micah 1:2)

Several times in the OT mountains are personified
(i.e. 2 Sam. 1:21; Ps. 68:15-16; Isa. 35:1). These mountains and hills were the very places (i.e. "high places") Ba'al and
Asherah were worshiped.

Special Topic: Fertility Worship of the ANE

6:2 This verse is legal imagery. YHWH turns from addressing His people, Judah, to address
the permanent, foundational, personified witnesses, the mountains and hills.

▣ "His people" Privilege (covenant people, cf. Micah 6:3; Rom. 9:4-5) brings responsibility
(cf. Luke 12:48)! This is parallel in the next line with "Israel," which is the collective designation of the covenant people.

Special Topic: Covenant

Special Topic: Israel (the name)

▣ "Even with Israel He will dispute" This does not refer to the Northern Ten Tribes (i.e. Israel) only
(cf. Micah 6:16), but here to all of the tribes, the descendants of Jacob (Israel). There are consequences for
covenant disobedience.

6:3-5 YHWH asks His people why, when He has been faithful, they have continued to be rebellious. YHWH
is using a covenant treaty pattern (i.e. Hittite Suzerain Treaties of the second millennium B.C.,
which also form the outline of the book of Deuteronomy and Joshua 24) to recall His faithful acts.

Special Topic: Hittite (Suzerain) Treaties

Special Topic: Stubbornness

6:3 "what have I done to you" YHWh asks them to bring their complaints or charges against Him (cf. Jer. 2:5). Where,
when, how has He not been faithful to His covenant responsibilities?

▣ "Answer Me" This is a legal term (BDB 772, KB 851, Qal IMPERATIVE), which means
"to give evidence against" (cf. Exod. 20:16; Deut. 5:20; 2 Sam. 1:16). YHWH is acting as one party in a divorce case.

6:4 "I brought you up. . .Egypt" This refers to YHWH's promise to Abraham in Gen. 15:6 and relates to the
events of the exodus. The exodus is the foundational act of YHWH's redemption in the history of national Israel (cf. Exod. 20:2; Deut. 5:6; 7:8).
This event clearly showed YHWH's faithful commitment to His covenant responsibilities (i.e. Amos 2:10; 3:1; 9:7). God's
grace came before the Mosaic law.

Special Topic: Characteristics of Israel's God (OT)

▣ "ransomed" This word literally means "to buy back" (BDB 804, KB 911, Qal PERFECT). It
was used in the sense of buying someone back from slavery or a from being prisoner of war. This concept becomes a key theological term.
The opposition idiom would be God "sold" them!

Special Topic: Ransom/Redeem

▣ "I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam" YHWH had provided the needed revelations and godly leadership, but
His people had rebelled, even during the exodus. His people have a track record of rebellion (cf. Stephen's sermon in Acts 7).

Notice Miriam is mentioned in a parallel way to Moses and Aaron. The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1214, says "Miriam, here, plays
a role equal to her brothers."

Special Topic: Women in the Bible

Special Topic: Ways of Revelation

6:5 "remember now" This (BDB 269, KB 269) is a Qal IMPERATIVE. YHWH wants His
covenant people to remember an earlier time of testing and revelation (i.e. Num. 22:5-6).

It is interesting that in the OT, YHWH is called on to forget (i.e. their sin), but His people to remember (His word)!

▣ "Balak. . .Balaam" This event is recorded in Numbers 22-25. See my exegetical notes there online,
www.freebiblecommentary.org

▣ "Shittim" This was the last camping site of Israel before entering the Promised Land. It is also the
scene of the sin of Israel with Moabite women (i.e. fertility worship, cf. Num. 33:49).

▣ "Gilgal" This was the first camping site within the Promised Land (cf. Joshua 4:19). Even in the
midst of their sin and rebellion at Shittim, YHWH forgave them and brought them safely through the raging, flooding
Jordan River into the Promised Land.

Taken together the mentioning of these two locations would imply the miraculous crossing of
the Jordan River during its flooding season (cf. Joshua 3).

▣ "the righteous acts of the Lord" Righteousness is a key theological concept.

Special Topic: Righteousness

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: MICAH 6:6-8

6With what shall I come to the Lord

And bow myself before the God on high?

Shall I come to Him with burnt offerings,

With yearling calves?

7Does the Lord take delight in thousands of rams,

In ten thousand rivers of oil?

Shall I present my first-born for my rebellious acts,

The fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?

8He has told you, O man, what is good;

And what does the Lord require of you

But to do justice, to love kindness,

And to walk humbly with your God?

6:6-7 In verses 6-7 the literary form of diatribe (i.e. a supposed objector) is used. There is a series
of questions by the covenant people. YHWH answers these in v. 8. The prophet uses a supposed collective person to voice the false views
which were commonly held by the people of Judah. They thought YHWH was being unfair to them and that He only wanted more sacrifices.

There is a good discussion in Ancient Israel, pp. 454-456, by Roland deVaux about the texts in the OT that seem
to reject sacrifices as the will of God.

Special Topic: YHWH's Covenant Requirements of Israel

6:6 "With what shall I come to the Lord" This is a crucial question. Judah thought the sacrificial system
(i.e. Lev. 1-7) was the key. The system was not the problem. It had been given by YHWH. The problem was ritual and liturgy without heart felt
faith and worth, accompanied by a lifestyle that neglected and disregarded the other aspects of the Mosaic legislation. Judah took the system
as the goal instead of a growing covenant love for God that issues in covenant love for His people (i.e. v. 8; 1 Sam. 15:22; Ps. 51:16-17; Prov. 21:3.
The NT counterpoint would be Jesus' words in Matt. 22:36-40; Mark 12:28-34; Luke 10:25-28).

Think of what moderns bring to God and think they are accepted!

▣

"the God on high"

NKJV, Peshitta
"the High God"

NRSV, JPSOA
"God on high"

TEV
"the God of heaven"

NJB
"God All-high"

"to my God Most HIgh"

"the sovereign God"

This (BDB 43 CONSTRUCT BDB 928) is imagery for "the Most High God"
or "exalted God" (cf. Ps. 99:2; 113:4; 38:6; Isa. 57:15). Here, it refers to YHWH, but not in a polytheistic pantheon.
He is alone, unique. The only True God!

Special Topic: Monotheism

Special Topic: Names for Deity, A.

▣ "yearling calves" These were unblemished calves (characteristic markings of the species) used for sacrifice
from the age of eight days to one year (cf. Lev. 9:3 and 22:27).

6:7 "in thousands of rams. . .rivers of oil" The people are

- charging YHWH of being unreasonable in His requirements. However, He never asked for these things. They
reflect pagan worship practices.

- on some national occasions large numbers of sacrifices are given (i.e. dedication of Solomon's temple,
i.e. 1 Kgs. 8:63).

Could this representative speaker be talking of an event of national repentance (i.e. ritual sacrifice)?

▣ "first-born. . .fruit of my body" Is this a purposeful distortion (i.e. hyperbole) or a sincere misunderstanding
of Genesis 22 or Exod. 13:2-12? There are several places in the Mosaic Law where human sacrifice is condemned
(cf. Lev. 18:21; 20:2-5; Deut. 12:31; 18:10; Ps. 106:37; Jer. 7:31).

It is possible that YHWH's people had become so spiritually confused that they attempted to worship
Him in the form of Molech, the fertility fire god of Ammon (cf. Lev. 18:21; 20:2-5; 1 Kgs. 11:7; 2 Kgs. 3:27; 16:3;
17:17; 21:6; 23:10; Jer. 32:35; Amos 5:26; Acts 7:43).

YHWH's people attempted to save the nation by offering an innocent one ("child"). In some way they
had logically extended the sacrificial system (cf. Lev. 1-7) in an inappropriate direction. However, it is this
same concept that lies behind Genesis 22 and Calvary (cf. Isa. 53; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21).

Special Topic: Molech

6:8 "He has told you" The VERB (BDB 616, KB 665) is a Hiphil PERFECT
and may reflect Micah 6:4. God had provided a revelation of His character and will (esp. as it related to sacrifice,
cf. 1 Sam. 15:22; Ps. 51:16-17; Isa. 1:11-17; Hosea 6:5-6). This verse seems to reflect a comment of Micah.

▣ "soul" See Special Topic: Nephesh

▣ "O, man" This VOCATIVE is addressing the idolatrous covenant people of Judah. This
verse is not addressing how Gentiles might be saved (i.e. works righteousness), but how covenant people must live
in grateful response to YHWH's forgiveness (which in the OT was symbolized as the sacrifice of an innocent animal,
cf. John 1:29; 2 Cor. 5:21). For a good brief discussion of this topic see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 336-337.

▣ "what is good" This verse is the most well known saying of the book of Micah. It refers to the priority of loving, interpersonal
relationships on a high level of care and love (cf. Ps. 14:1,3; 37:3; 51:17; Hosea 12:6 and described in Ps. 15:2-5), not cultic
performance (i.e. sacrifice) only (cf. Isa. 1:13; Amos 5:21-23).

This verse is a wonderful definition of what OT "good" (BDB 373 II) is in YHWH's eyes
(cf. Micah 3:2; Isa. 1:17; 5:20; Amos 5:14-15). This definition of "good" matches Rom. 8:28, explained in v. 29 as Christlikeness.

▣ "require" This VERB (BDB 205, KB 233) is a Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE,
which represents continuous action. The term means "to demand" or "ask for" (i.e. Deut. 18:19; 23:21).

▣ "justice" In this context "justice" (BDB 1048, see
Special Topic: Justice) refers to social
fairness, which is discussed in Micah 6:9-11. The OT knows no distinction between the secular and the sacred! All of life
is sacred! See note at Micah 3:1.

There is a series of three Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS:

- "Do justice" (BDB 793, KB 889; see Special Topic: Justice)

- "Love kindness" (BDB 12, KB 17; see Special Topic: Lovingkindness)

- "Walk humbly" (BDB 229, KB 246; see Special Topic: The Path, The Way)

Biblical faith affects every aspect of daily life. Faith is a lifestyle, not just a theology or creed (i.e. Eph. 1:4; 2:10. The
divine covenant gift of eternal life (i.e. the restoration of the image and likeness of God damaged in the fall) has observable
characteristics (both in relation to God and other humans). This verse is one of the best in the OT describing these
characteristics.

▣ "love kindness" This is the powerful covenant word hesed (BDB 338). It refers to YHWH's
covenant loyalty. It reflects His sacrificial, no-strings-attached, covenant love. I think this term, in many ways,
is analogous in meaning to the NT agapē.

Special Topic: Lovingkindness (hesed)

Special Topic: Love (agapē)

▣ "walk humbly" This is an acknowledgment of

- human need (i.e. possible meaning of this rare word "humble" (BDB 857, KB 1039, INFINITIVE
ABSOLUTE, cf. Prov. 11:2, found only here)

- human lifestyle guided by YHWH's revelation (i.e. Mosaic covenant requirements)

Ritual without the proper attitude (cf. Isa. 29:13 vs. 57:15 and 66:2d) is an
abomination (cf. 1 Sam. 15:22; Matt. 23:23).

"Walk" in the Bible is

- imagery of fellowship with someone (i.e. Gen. 5:24; 6:9; Job 34:8; Ps. 1:1; Mal. 2:6)

- imagery for daily living (cf. Eph. 4:1,17; 5:2,15)

Biblical faith is daily (not weekly or annually), personal relationship directed toward YHWH
and other human beings! Biblical faith has observable characteristics. It is both what not to do but also what to do!

Special Topic: The Path, The Way

▣ "will not anoint yourself with oil" Olive oil had many purposes in ANE. One of them
was to rub on the skin in preparation of a social event. It was a symbol of happiness and joy. The lack of oil was seen
as a divine judgment (cf. Deut. 28:40).

6:16 "Omri" This was a politically effective king of Israel (i.e. 876-869 B.C., cf. 1 Kgs. 16:21-28). His name
became the common name for the Northern Ten Tribes in the Assyrian records (i.e. "House of Omri"). This title became an
idiom for their godless living. It came to characterize Judah also in v. 6, line 3 (cf. Micah 1:9, i.e. 2 Kgs. 17:19,22)!

Special Topic: Kings of the Divided Kingdom

and Asherah into Samarian society (i.e. 869-850 B.C., cf. 1 Kgs. 16:29-34; 18; 21:25).

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.
